value.definition: Tier-1 document owning bounded-work procedure: steps, transitions, intake, execution units, admission, applicability and exclusion, output, configurations, delegation, context construction and fit, acquisition, activation, evaluation, derived-surface staleness, result refinements, disposition, totality, refinement, licensing, work state, restart, proportionality, resource limits, closed results and reuse. It uses, without redefining, the objects and result algebra owned by FOUNDATIONS and the frame object and activate outcomes owned by REFERENCE_FRAME.

grounding.quote:
it redefines nothing those
members own.

value.label: ACTIVATION document

value.definition: Activation of one reference frame or one declared active frame configuration on an exact subject. Its context is the activated frame's projection to the actor, never the corpus or workspace. Intake, admission, applicability and activation remain distinct even within one invocation.

grounding.quote:
Intake, admission,
applicability and activation are distinct relations inside the step even
when one invocation performs all of them.

value.label: Step

value.definition: Source-authored foundation-to-law traces distinguish premises, their standing, consequences, owning rules, added domain or policy choices, pillars and consumers. The transitions/steps/configuration family covers §§1 and 4; the work-state/resumption/reuse family covers §§5 and 7. These traces describe the subject's reasoning and ownership, not a derivation performed by this interpretation.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs,
not commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

value.label: Foundation-to-law traces

value.definition: Material workspace state and authoritative inputs together with justified knowledge and explicit unknowns. Work state records its workspace, governing basis, still-applicable closed results and judgments, residuals and uncertainty about external effects. An actor's context is an account of this state, not the state itself.

grounding.quote:
An actor's context is an account of the
current state, not the state itself

value.label: Current state

value.definition: Owner-defined constraints comprising the selected outcome, its acceptance conditions and governing obligations to preserve. Multiple realised states may satisfy it. Construction denotes this predicate by Z; its governing specification supplies it through the selected WHAT across Intent, Product and Specification, whose descriptions refine it.

grounding.quote:
It names no single
state: its acceptance conditions admit several realised states.

The
governing specification, the selected WHAT across the Intent, Product and
Specification of the Product that owns the work, supplies Z; its
descriptions refine Z.

value.label: Destination

value.definition: Bounded change from current to next state carried out by one step. Work fitting one activation has one transition; work exceeding it is refined into bounded transitions, each with its own step, under §4. Each binds applicable outer destination obligations and obligations of affected governing relations.

grounding.quote:
A transition is a bounded change from the current state to a next state,
carried out by one step.

value.label: Transition

value.definition: The corpus's single owning construction relation binds current state A and destination Z, selects work, composes steps, corrects discrepancies and supports completion claims. It is described as carrying the owning Product's common construction requirement and universal construction model. Its consumers apply it without establishing a second relation.

grounding.quote:
This subsection states the construction relation for this corpus: how a
selected construction binds its current state and destination, chooses
its work, composes its steps, corrects itself and claims completion.

value.label: Construction relation

value.definition: Three distinct subject accounts: specification models required conditions; observations describe what holds; a causal or predictive model explains possible state changes from actions. These differ from FOUNDATIONS' accounts of a construction. Each can be incomplete or wrong differently; predictive-model applicability and adequacy are separate claims.

grounding.quote:
The specification is the internal reference model of the required
conditions. Observations describe what does hold. A causal or
predictive model explains how an action may change the state.

value.label: Specification, observations and predictive model

value.definition: Arrangement of admissible construction and assurance serving Z within a selected resource envelope. Selection belongs to the realisation and actor exercising admitted work authority. A composition boundary connects a step's output to the next starting state; it is distinct from a categorical join, which maps categories. Feedback observes, compares governing conditions, diagnoses discrepancies, selects an authorised response, acts and observes again; homeostasis is corrective activity, not guaranteed convergence.

grounding.quote:
A strategy arranges admissible construction and assurance to
serve Z within the selected resource envelope.

A composition boundary is the boundary between
successive steps, where one step's output becomes the next step's
starting state.

Homeostasis
means correction towards the required conditions as disturbances and new
observations arise; it guarantees neither convergence nor the adequacy of
those conditions.

value.label: Strategy, composition and feedback

value.definition: Exact step input contract sufficient to reconstruct governing relations without conversation history, commentary or previous-actor memory. It identifies governed work, subject and basis, permitted inputs, evaluation and result algebra, affected relations and invariants, admission relations, shared computational machinery and binding, authorities and grants, actor envelopes, invalidators, re-entry conditions and applicable cost-claim allowance and spend measurement.

grounding.quote:
A step is activated from an intake sufficient to reconstruct its governing
relations without conversation history, commentary or a prior actor's memory

value.label: Intake

value.definition: Smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing relation. It need not align with a function, file, module, ticket field or design document. It supplies §2's seed set Z, whose projection is context; this seed-set notation is distinct from construction's destination predicate Z.

grounding.quote:
The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable
of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing
relation.

value.label: Execution unit

value.definition: Step contract whose drafting and admission are distinct relations, including inside one invocation. Minimum states are drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded. Its admitted result identifies admission mechanism and authority, exact contract identity or digest, decision and evidence, including any human override; it names one durable result and evidence surface.

grounding.quote:
A contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and
superseded

value.label: Execution contract and admission

value.definition: Evaluation of whether an obligation applies to the exact subject, owned by the evaluation and scope declarations and decided from sufficient basis-bound facts. Exclusion is the state of an obligation after falsified applicability, not a result of that obligation. Unresolved applicability is distinct from exclusion.

grounding.quote:
An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
`falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value

value.label: Applicability and exclusion

value.definition: Candidate plus step-produced facts: judgments and evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance and one construction-availability stop state. The actor's internal path is excluded from output and is not governed.

grounding.quote:
The step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts: judgments with
their evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance, and
one stop state, a value of construction availability (§3).

value.label: Step output

value.definition: Task-wide allocation of responsibilities and information exchanges to frames; activation binds actors to frames. Its active frame configuration is the part used for one evaluation or decision. Allocation derives from operations, dependencies, actor capabilities and required assurance, which constrain but do not determine its arrangement.

grounding.quote:
A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2).

value.label: Configuration

value.definition: Roles are allocated relations over steps, not actor kinds or a fixed inventory. Where present, constructor owns bounded implementation and self-review, assessor independently evaluates a frozen candidate, and decision owner disposes. Other responsibilities may be allocated. A bounded proxy has only the acceptance and advancement permissions declared by the governing authority relation.

grounding.quote:
Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.

value.label: Roles and bounded delegation

value.definition: Source-described procedure taking seed set Z of intake subject, outcome and affected relations, dependency family R whose changes can alter result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority, and actor envelope B. It computes material closure, projects with recorded seams, tests fit and acquires declared inputs. Context capacity bounds what can be held; attention bounds what can be used.

grounding.quote:
Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the
intake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can
alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and
the actor's envelope B:

value.label: Context construction under an envelope

value.definition: Read-only observation of frame, subject and declared inputs within intake-permitted acquisition. Acquisition is neither admission nor a further actor stage and confers no role, operation or decision. Activation binds reusable frame declarations to exact subject and basis and loads declared material relations and evidence sources. Evaluation applies the activated frame's invariants, evidence rules and result algebra.

grounding.quote:
Acquisition is the read-only observation of the material a
step needs (its frame, its subject and its declared inputs) within the
inputs its intake permits it to acquire

value.label: Acquisition, activation and evaluation

value.definition: Material copied, projected or compressed from owning sources, including task-projected frames and a current a_c interpretation's task constraint surface. It names its sources and owns no determination. Currentness, fidelity and question-specific sufficiency are distinct.

grounding.quote:
A derived surface is material derived from owning
sources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame
for a task; it names its sources and owns no determination.

- Matching source identities establish only that the surface was derived
  from those sources. They establish neither its fidelity to them nor its
  sufficiency for a question; a surface found insufficient for a named
  question is handled as Acquisition above states.

value.label: Derived surface

value.definition: Prompt as rendered contract over typed authority, not source law. It projects current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and fallback conditions needed by the step.

grounding.quote:
A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;
it is not source law.

value.label: Prompt contract

value.definition: Five source-defined refinements of the core, each answering a different predicate: admission/activation—lawful beginning on exact subject and basis; construction availability—candidate available; disposition—candidate accepted at declared boundary; ambiguity outcome—declared ambiguity resolved on exact basis; effects—intended effect occurred.

grounding.quote:
Each names the question it answers and the
predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
core value

value.label: Predicate-bound result refinements

value.definition: Pre-step outcome domain for lawful admission and activation on exact subject and basis: activated, admission_refused(authority), admission_refused(basis), closure_unresolved, out_of_frame and activation_refusal with its cause. Frame-activation causes and mappings remain owned by REFERENCE_FRAME §5.

grounding.quote:
The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values.

value.label: Admission and activation outcomes

conditions: A step has been lawfully activated.
value.definition: Output-existence domain: candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested(authority), re_entry_requested(basis). Output is the constructed subject for a constructing step or closed results for an assessing step; it remains a candidate until evaluated.

grounding.quote:
A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
assessing step.

value.label: Construction availability

conditions: A decision owner disposes an assessed candidate.
value.definition: Acceptance-result domain comprising accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject. It consumes candidate availability and assessment results while remaining separate from both. An assessor's recommendation is decision evidence, never a disposition.

grounding.quote:
An assessor may recommend one; the
recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition

value.label: Candidate disposition

conditions: An ambiguity is declared.
value.definition: Recorded resolution-status domain comprising resolved, carried, escalated and blocked, mapped for whether that ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis.

grounding.quote:
A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
outcome is recorded either way

value.label: Ambiguity outcome

conditions: A step has an intended external effect.
value.definition: Evidence-bound effect-outcome domain: completed, not_effected and completion_unknown, for attainment of the declared intended outcome. Whether the effect has ended is a separate question. An effect of uncertain completion is completion_unknown or not_effected with its end unestablished.

grounding.quote:
An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred"

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established.

value.label: External effect and end status

value.definition: Advance declaration of next moves for every admitted condition class, including an explicit unknown class. Handling options are supported continuation within contract, refinement, recovery, yield, owning-relation re-entry and termination. Hard stops are conditions that halt work regardless of ambiguity-policy risk appetite.

grounding.quote:
Each admitted condition class has a declared
next move, including an explicit unknown class.

value.label: Total handling and hard stops

value.definition: Refinement decomposes an outer transformation T: A → X into typed steps carrying success predicates P₀ … Pₙ. Rewrite replaces a representation, step or composite with another claimed to preserve meaning. A licensing law is an owner-declared law permitting the operation. Exact steps preserve declared meaning; approximate steps instead require an adequacy relation and an argued composite end-to-end bound.

grounding.quote:
An outer transformation T: A → X with success predicates P₀ … Pₙ
is faithfully refined by steps Tᵢ

A rewrite step replaces a representation, a step or
a composite by another that is claimed to keep its meaning

value.label: Refinement, rewrite and licensing

conditions: The transition is material.
value.definition: Each admission owner's independent derivation and validation of the complete enclosing relation from authoritative inputs. The relation includes every participant and equality join whose identity, validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by admission, plus relevant crossing-seam far sides unless authoritatively excluded.

grounding.quote:
each admission owner is independently
responsible for deriving and validating the complete enclosing relation
from authoritative inputs

value.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

value.definition: Qualification of the admission law for every admission owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design. Case applicability follows supported inputs, states and operating or threat model, with explicit observations for direct, composite/nested, forged, ambiguous, stale, mixed-basis, competing-authority, reconstruction, replay and atomic-publication cases.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of the admission law is instantiated for every admission
owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design

value.label: Standing structural qualification

value.definition: Persistent object tuple: current workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with invalidators, residuals and known uncertainty over external effects. Carrier choice belongs to profile or realisation; resumption, checkpointing and progress accounting are generic procedures. Resumption re-enters the same method on current material state, possibly with another actor.
value.label: Work state and resumption

value.definition: Acceptance binds an exact checkpoint. A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted work under an existing exact operation grant but is not acceptance, promotion or publication. Restart reconstructs from less than retained work. Progress categories are accepted material movement, prerequisite work, evidence that is not new progress, churn and forecast revision; these are semantic categories, not a numerical algorithm.

grounding.quote: Acceptance binds one exact checkpoint.

These are
semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm

value.label: Checkpoint, restart and progress categories

value.definition: The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations. Their current material state is the continuing truth surface deciding what work has and has not occurred; work state and closed results carry continuity without requiring another carrier.

grounding.quote:
The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
material state decides what the work has and has not done.

value.label: Workspace truth surface

value.definition: An actor's context is a bounded projection and revisable account of work state, disposable because required step-produced facts and closed results are recorded before return. It is never a second truth surface; later intake reconstructs governing relations without needing the previous actor's context.

grounding.quote:
An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).

value.label: Actor's account

value.definition: Proportionality relates semantic ambiguity removed to effective reasoning complexity introduced. Complexity includes independent concepts and authority surfaces, joins, exceptions, branching, states, transitions, duplicated representations needing reconciliation and decision-relevant detail; it is not raw line, artifact or context-window size. Cost is selected when it is the governed question.

grounding.quote:
Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and
effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is
proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space
justifies the additional concepts, relations, projections and evidence an
actor must hold together to reach a correct decision

value.label: Proportionality and selected cost

value.definition: A resource limit bounds activation consumption of context, attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or machine resources. This subsection owns the generic declaration, measurement and exhaustion law, but sets no limit value; selected execution bindings supply values and measurable units and boundaries.

grounding.quote:
A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

value.label: Declared resource limit

value.definition: A closed result identifies frame, activation, subject, basis, evaluation, actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. It supports handoff and exact-applicability reuse without requiring private working context. Its affectedness is expressed by dependencies D*(t) meeting change impact cover I(Δ).

grounding.quote:
A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions

value.label: Closed result and reuse

value.definition: Transition evidence is a consumer-represented read model of an exact candidate, affected relations, changed realisation paths, added or removed authority paths, retained and open seams, focused and required integration proofs, explicit non-changes, any activated assessor's recommended disposition and the decision owner's disposition once made.

grounding.quote:
Consumers
choose the representation. Transition evidence is a read
model; it does not become specification, design or admission authority

value.label: Transition evidence

value.definition: The source-disposition register records claimed conservation, new successor rules, ownership routes, generalisations, exceptions and pending replacements relative to rc.2. Its foundation-to-law tables distinguish derived consequences from owned policy choices and decide nothing. Register statements are provenance and proposal data, not this interpretation's acceptance of equivalence or supersession.

grounding.quote: a table decides nothing and names the rule that states each consequence.

value.label: Activation source-disposition register

value.definition: ASSURANCE is a tier-2 owner of verification layers, testing taxonomy and two proof authorities, fixture portability, test authority, scenarios, installed proof, significant paths, testing frames, combinatorial value, legitimate-path erasure, evidence composition, subject acquisition, localisation and interface integration. It consumes tier-1 laws without redefining them. SPEC_METHOD owns the particular chain/change classes; PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns project bindings. Design-module and ticket test authority are not pre-empted. EXECUTIVE_BASELINE maps roles at tier 3 and is not a dependency. Predecessor routes are provenance only; the standalone successor claims to restate received rows fully.

grounding.quote:
[EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md) (claims, separation, independent
assessment, acceptance, conformance) and [ACTIVATION](ACTIVATION.md)
(§1 applicability and the execution relation, §6 proportionality, §7
reuse); adds no definition to tier 1.

value.label: ASSURANCE member

value.definition: Requirements preserve invariant truth and ask what must be true; design preserves structural choice and asks how that truth is realised; scenarios preserve operational meaning and ask whether the realised system can do the claimed thing. Scenarios are the product-owner layer of concrete end-to-end use cases from intent to realised behaviour.

grounding.quote:
| Requirements | invariant truth | what must be true? |
| Design | structural choice | how is that truth realised? |
| Scenarios | operational meaning | can the realised system actually do the claimed thing? |

value.label: Verification layers

value.definition: F14 organises evidence for claims about realised products. Its instance premises, not supplied by commitments, are a runnable/observable product in source and runnable forms; composition across modules, interfaces and owners; user outcomes on supported surfaces; possible external worker/transport/fixture boundaries; and optionally design-governed module boundaries. The table accounts for §§1–16; §17 records dispositions and decides nothing. It distinguishes consequences, domain/policy choices and their owners.

grounding.quote:
decides what evidence proves a claim about a realised product and how
that evidence is organised. Its instance premises, which the commitments
do not supply, are named in the rows as follows: runnable product, a
product's realisation can be executed or observed, in a source form and in
a deployed, installed or otherwise runnable form, to produce evidence;

value.label: F14 foundation-to-law family

value.definition: The Product-level test-authority taxonomy belongs to urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance under the selected complete basis. Its two primary authorities are design/module conformance, derived from realisation authority, and UAT/acceptance, derived from constitutional user/Product authority. Unit denotes conformance scope; integration denotes breadth; sandbox denotes composed-product acceptance execution; harnessed/fake/recorded/deterministic denote non-live execution; live denotes real external worker or transport execution. Shared context does not merge DESIGN_MODULE's module-derived unit-proof authority.

grounding.quote:
Authority source is not execution breadth. A test may be small or broad,
fast or slow, deterministic or live, and still derives from one of two
primary authorities (P6, P1):

1. design or module conformance tests; and
2. UAT, or acceptance, tests.

value.label: Testing authority taxonomy

value.definition: Fixture and proof portability makes required closure lanes reproducible from their declared source boundary and distinguishes missing-fixture diagnostics from product semantic failure.

grounding.quote:
Required closure lanes are reproducible from the declared source boundary
(P3, P6; rc.2 #fixture-and-proof-portability-rule). A unit, semantic or
module-design conformance lane does not depend on an undeclared local path,
a sibling workspace, an operator home directory or a mutable external
fixture.

value.label: Fixture and proof portability

value.definition: Written, traceable test-case authority for every live requirement includes appropriate scenario bundles, ordered sequences, negative/control or other explicit evidence cases. Each expected result's assertion provenance identifies its owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation, shared dependencies, and whether its predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction.

grounding.quote:
Written authority includes the assertion
provenance of each expected result: the owning obligation, its
interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies, and
whether the asserted predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition of
it or part of a sufficient conjunction

value.label: Written test-case authority

value.definition: A scenario bundle exposes the feature/use-case boundary, ordered test-case sequence and expected outcomes at significant steps, making operational meaning inspectable. Declared scenarios pressure intent and design to identify operational boundaries, sequences, actors, controls and outcomes; the source calls them the best source for significant code/control paths.

grounding.quote:
A scenario bundle shows the feature or use-case boundary being exercised,
the test-case sequence that proves it, and the outcomes expected at each
significant step. It is the layer that makes operational meaning
inspectable (P6).

value.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.
value.definition: Installed development proof is the decisive proving lane against an installed development version treated as an independent project or externalised target.

grounding.quote:
Where a system has an installable or runnable development form, the
decisive proving lane runs against an installed development version as if
it were an independent project or an externalised target, not only against
the source tree in place

value.label: Installed development proof

value.definition: Significant-path coverage intentionally declares and proves meaningful paths for the claimed behaviour, rather than every branch in every file. Usual relevant paths are intended success; fail-closed/rejection; boundary/control; integration/dispatch/transport; recovery/retry/replay.

grounding.quote:
The proving surface declares and exercises the significant paths for the
behaviour being claimed (P6, P2; rc.2 #significant-path-coverage-rule).
Exhaustive proof does not mean every possible branch in every file; it
means the project names the meaningful paths and proves them
intentionally. The significant paths usually include, where relevant:

value.label: Significant-path coverage

conditions: The governing frame configuration or admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion, closure or release-assurance claim.
value.definition: The Product testing frame set is a claim-relative configuration ordinarily containing user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration and unit frames. Its document placement makes the set and §§8–13 available without adoption or automatic activation. Claim, subject, path, population, oracle and falsification boundary select a frame, not its runner.

grounding.quote: ## 7. Product testing frame set

Placement in this member makes the
set, and the law of §8 to §13 that serves it, available; it adopts nothing,
and each activation is decided by ACTIVATION §1 (Applicability). The kind
of runner does not select the frame; the evaluated claim, subject, path,
population, oracle and falsification boundary do

value.label: Product testing frame set

value.definition: A testing frame executes or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim using an explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification condition. Mere files, suites, runners, fixtures, labels, coverage percentages or actors are not thereby frames; counts, coverage, duration and framework category do not widen the actually exercised claim's authority.

grounding.quote:
A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes
or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an
explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification

ASSURANCE consumes through the explicit binding; UX refinements apply to UX surfaces; recurrence refines TICKETS §6; selection refines FOUNDATIONS Shared machinery; ACTIVATION Intake consumes frame evidence only for governed boundaries.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

value.label: Declared rule consumers and ownership direction

conditions: The profile operates inside a graph-execution-governed Product.
value.definition: A deterministic module is a realisation cut inside the graph program. Review first identifies whether the boundary is an operative graph traversal. Typed asset-state movement follows outcome traversal, then declarative graph carriers (GTL and ABG), then deterministic module realisation.

grounding.quote:
If the boundary represents product
movement from one typed asset state to another, the governing shape is:

1. outcome traversal under the graph-execution profile;
2. the declarative graph carrier structure (GTL and ABG in that profile's
   terms); and
3. deterministic module realisation under this profile.

value.label: Graph traversal and deterministic realisation alignment

conditions: The profile governs the changed boundary.
value.definition: Three overriding boundary-closure evaluators: authority seam closure, essential carrier consolidation and enforcement after proof. Each design or implementation change should be judged against them; they are not optional heuristics. Better ergonomics, tests or static-checker output with failure of an evaluator is not real progress under the profile.

grounding.quote:
When this profile governs a boundary, each design or implementation change
should be judged against three overriding evaluators (P6, P2;
rc.2 #3b-boundary-closure-evaluators). They are not optional heuristics. A
change that improves local ergonomics, test output or static-checker
output but fails one of them is not real progress under this profile.

value.label: Overriding boundary-closure evaluators

value.definition: Closure of a semantic authority seam requires one authoritative carrier or contract, with no surviving silent reconstruction path when that carrier is removed. Query and projection closure additionally includes coherence with named admitted source truth.

grounding.quote:
The test: if the authoritative carrier
were removed, would the system fail closed, or would another path silently
reconstruct the same meaning? If meaning survives by reconstruction, the
seam is not closed.

value.label: Authority seam closure

value.definition: Consolidation toward the few real identity-bearing carrier families, beginning with declared IACS and default subordination of Subordinate Payloads. Its progress measure is sharper/fewer families, less duplicate authority and less boundary inflation, rather than additional wrappers, branch-local peer types or public records mirroring payload details.

grounding.quote:
Each change should collapse the slice to the few real identity-bearing
carrier families (P3, P2; rc.2 #2-essential-carrier-consolidation). This
means declaring the IACS first (§6), keeping Subordinate Payloads
subordinate by default, and avoiding fragment classes, interfaces or result
records created only to satisfy typing, serialisation or convenience
extraction. Progress is fewer, sharper carrier families, less duplicate
authority and less boundary inflation; not one more wrapper layer, one more
branch-local peer type, or one more public record that only mirrors
payload detail.

value.label: Essential carrier consolidation

value.definition: Language-independent sequence: parse, validate or construct; explicitly admit and narrow; then enforce the already-proved shape with typing, schemas, validators, contracts or codecs. Examples include mypy --strict, sealed algebraic type plus parser, or compiler-enforced sum type plus decoder.

grounding.quote:
Typing, schemas, validators, contracts and codecs exist to lock in a seam
that has already been made real (P6, P1; rc.2 #3-enforcement-after-proof).
Parse, validate or construct first; admit and narrow the boundary
explicitly; then use types or schemas to enforce the proved shape.

value.label: Proof before enforcement

value.definition: Ingress conversion receives foreign input, parses/validates/normalises once, constructs admitted local carrier truth, and exposes only that local truth to semantic kernels.
value.label: Ingress collapse

conditions: The profile governs repo-authored Python at the adopted boundary.
value.definition: Python semantic design uses fully annotated callable parameters/returns and closed typed carriers, including tests, scripts and support code at the production bar. Closed forms may include dataclass, TypedDict, Protocol, Literal, Enum or equivalents. Strict static checking, such as mypy --strict or an equivalent strict configuration, is required.

grounding.quote:
When this profile governs a Python boundary, repo-authored Python is fully
typed (P1; rc.2 #4a-python-typing-rule): every function, method and
callable surface has explicit parameter and return annotations; semantic
carriers are closed and typed; and repo-authored tests, scripts and
support code are typed too, with no lower bar than production code.

value.label: Governed Python boundary

value.definition: Engineering Ontology of one designed boundary consists of entities, identities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle, authority, atomic functions, higher-order composition, effects and projections. Once accepted it is the prior semantic-design authority, subordinate to constitutional intent, Product, requirements and applicable graph/domain profiles. Accepted target design remains the structural HOW: topology, interfaces, carrier placement, module boundaries, algorithms and local realisation. A class, schema, endpoint, command or carrier inventory alone is not an Ontology.

grounding.quote:
Ontology =
  entities + identities + relationships + invariants + lifecycle
  + authority + atomic functions + higher-order composition
  + effects + projections

value.label: Ontology and accepted semantic basis

conditions: For one governed boundary B.
value.definition: U(B) is the unresolved subset of complete material relations M(B). decision_complete(B) holds iff U(B) is empty, M(B) is jointly satisfiable, and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations. co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B). design_gate(B) is the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish decision completeness.

grounding.quote:
U(B) = unresolved(M(B))
decision_complete(B) iff
  U(B) = empty
  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable
  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the
      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations
co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)
design_gate(B) =
  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish
  decision_complete(B)

value.label: Decision completeness and proportional sequencing

conditions: For one governed boundary B.
value.definition: M(B) includes entities, identities, relationships, cardinalities, invariants, authorities, authority transitions, functions, higher-order composition laws, topology, lifecycle states/transitions, public contracts, externally observable Product meaning, declared domains/admission conditions, failure/refusal routes, effect/closure laws, projections, module mappings and material algorithmic obligations. Ontology, Prime contraction, IACS, target design, three views, public contracts, module boundaries, implementation and tests are projections of this single network at different reasoning altitudes.

grounding.quote:
M(B) =
  entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants
  + authorities + authority transitions + functions
  + higher-order composition laws + topology
  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts
  + externally observable Product meaning
  + declared domains and admission conditions
  + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws
  + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations

value.label: Complete material-relation network M(B)

value.definition: A material design frame declares its governing accepted frames/relations, proposed action's bounded affected relation set, inherited invariants, crossing authority/composition seams, and subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions. Global and local are relative to the selected frame. Governing frames form a constraint network, possibly with several parents rather than a compulsory hierarchy.
value.label: Bounded design frame

value.definition: Native constructability is the selected substrate's ability to construct the design's required identities, relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle, composition, publication and retirement behaviour. It is an acceptance obligation, not a prescribed implementation.

grounding.quote:
A semantically coherent design is not acceptable when its selected
substrate cannot natively construct the required identities,
relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle,
composition, publication and retirement behaviour (P2, P5;
rc.2 #native-constructability-before-design-acceptance-stdo-up-002). A missing
substrate capability remains an explicit design gap or triggers lawful
re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §4); it is not hidden behind a reference bridge,
adapter, filesystem runner, test double or promised future feature (P6;
SPEC_METHOD §7 Bridge prohibition). This is a constructability obligation,
not a prescribed implementation; the consumer chooses the substrate and the
evidence mechanism (P0).

value.label: Native constructability

conditions: Before constructing a material generic capability, common mechanic or algorithm, or selecting a material dependency.
value.definition: Proportional bounded foundation-selection procedure refining FOUNDATIONS §4 Shared machinery. It compares candidate compositions drawn from admitted project foundations; language/runtime/platform/standard-library capabilities; accepted predecessor or immutable-lineage realisations usable as evidence; maintained external foundations where dependencies are permitted; and bounded local implementation. Constructability alone does not establish local construction as best.
exceptions: No package survey or ledger is required for a trivial helper whose choice cannot materially affect authority, Product behaviour, lifecycle cost or the accepted design network.

grounding.quote:
The bounded candidate population draws applicable compositions from:
foundations already admitted in the current project; language, runtime,
platform or standard-library capabilities; accepted predecessor or
immutable-lineage realisations usable as evidence; maintained external
foundations where the Product permits a dependency; and a bounded local
implementation (P2).

value.label: Capability and foundation selection

conditions: Among lawful candidate compositions on the current declared basis.
value.definition: Dominance holds only if every material decision dimension is comparable or evidenced non-discriminating, one composition is no worse on every comparable dimension and strictly better on at least one. Material unknowns that could reverse this prevent dominance. Materially incomparable lawful candidates form an explicit undominated frontier.

grounding.quote:
One lawful candidate composition dominates another on the current basis
only when every material decision dimension is comparable or evidenced as
non-discriminating between them, it is no worse on every comparable
dimension, and it is strictly better on at least one. A material unknown
that could reverse the relation prevents dominance and remains a gap. A
dominated candidate cannot be selected unless new evidence or another
material dimension invalidates the dominance relation; therefore a local
rebuild of generic mechanics is inadmissible when an existing lawful
foundation composition dominates it. Unused feature breadth alone does not
establish dominance and may itself add lifecycle cost (P2, P6).

value.label: Evidence-bounded dominance and frontier

conditions: For identity-bearing entities and independently governed value families inside the active boundary.
value.definition: Logical-completeness matrix or equivalent closed representation identifies Entity, Identity, Authority owner, Declare/create, Read/project, Update/transition and Delete/retire, alongside Ontology relationships, cardinalities, invariants and lifecycle states. These are completeness questions rather than a mutable-CRUD mandate. Entity lifecycle describes domain states/transformations, distinct from ASSURANCE §16's build/release/deploy/observe/retire operational module lifecycle.
exceptions: Subordinate Payloads and value objects inherit their owner's lifecycle and authority without a ceremonial peer row unless they pass the Promotion Test.

grounding.quote:
The matrix applies to identity-bearing entities and independently governed
value families (P3, P2). A Subordinate Payload or value object inherits the
lifecycle and authority of its owning entity unless it passes the
Promotion Test (§6); it does not require a ceremonial peer lifecycle row.

value.label: Entity and lifecycle completeness matrix

conditions: For every Ontology function or lifecycle transition crossing a semantic, authority, admission, effect, persistence or public boundary.
value.definition: Authority is part of Ontology from design inception. Matrix or equivalent closed representation distinguishes Function/transition, Proposer, Evaluator, Verifier, Admitter, Executor, Projector and Retirement owner. It separates actor identity from authority, capability from admitted authority for the current basis, each operational role from the others, attribution from permission, and domain-meaning ownership from runtime-effect ownership.
exceptions: Pure subordinate helpers inherit their owning Ontology function's authority envelope and need no peer row unless crossing one of the specified boundaries.

grounding.quote:
The model distinguishes actor identity from authority; available
capability from authority admitted for the current basis; proposal from
evaluation, verification, admission, execution, projection and retirement;
attribution from permission; and ownership of domain meaning from
ownership of runtime effects (P6; FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds).

value.label: Ontology authority matrix

conditions: For every consequential entity-transition domain.
value.definition: Complete relation deciding which candidate transformation becomes durable entity truth, covering entity identity, predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession law. A matrix naming who admits does not establish this relation. Singularity attaches to the complete decision relation, not to one actor, callable or component.

grounding.quote:
For every consequential entity-transition domain, design evidence contains
the complete transformation-admission relation over entity identity,
predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision
cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession
law, through the authority matrix or an equivalent closed representation
(P6, P4b):

value.label: Complete transformation-admission relation

value.definition: The engineering Ontology of a designed boundary is its single semantic truth, from which atomic function families and downstream design projections derive.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6; rc.2 #ontology-projection-law).
These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:

value.label: Engineering Ontology

value.definition: The smallest parameterised atomic function families that make entity lifecycles logically complete. Their derivation matrix records discovered functionality, entity, atomic function or template, higher-order composition, effect class, required authority and disposition.

grounding.quote: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |

value.label: Atomic function family

conditions: The boundary has higher-order behaviour.
value.definition: An explicitly named governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories are unit or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and projection.

grounding.quote:
Where the boundary has higher-order behaviour, the Ontology names the
governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories include unit
or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
projection.

value.label: Composition and effect algebra

value.definition: An irreducible design relation—atomic function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure law or composition law—that cannot honestly be composed from other accepted atoms while preserving meaning. Prime is a semantic-design property, not a property established by implementation size, naming, typing or independent testability.

grounding.quote:
A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
meaning (P3, P1; rc.2 #prime-semantic-atoms-and-universal-domain).

value.label: Prime semantic atom

value.definition: Review and contraction of the complete candidate semantic-atom family and every proposed realisation projection, including identities, authority transitions, lifecycles, topology, functions, composition laws, effects and closure laws.

grounding.quote:
Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
each atom in isolation. The family includes every proposed identity,
authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, function, composition
law, effect and closure law. A function-and-carrier-only pass does not
establish whole-family Prime

value.label: Whole-family Prime contraction

value.definition: A downstream implementation or design unit projecting accepted semantic atoms. Prime-conformance applies to functions, classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules; other Ontology projections include diagrams, matrices, IACS, APIs, operation registers, SDK/CLI surfaces, schemas, codecs, manifests, catalogues, target architecture and test/proof inventories.

grounding.quote:
Prime-conformance applies to these realisation projections: functions,
classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules. Typed
closure by itself is not sufficient reason to create a new top-level type.

value.label: Realisation projection

value.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family carrying a boundary's real functionality and authority flow. It is the declared carrier inventory to which the cited assurance rules bind conformance tests and unit proof. Example roles include source truth, admission, execution, yielded/recovery, effect plan and public projection carriers.

grounding.quote:
Examples of irreducible architectural carrier roles (P3) include the source
truth carrier, admission carrier, execution carrier, yielded or recovery
carrier, effect plan carrier and public projection carrier.

- Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS): the smallest lawful
  top-level carrier family required for one boundary;

value.label: Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set

value.definition: Payload detail inside a boundary that is not top-level by default.

grounding.quote:
- Subordinate Payload: payload detail that exists inside that boundary but
  is not top-level by default;

value.label: Subordinate Payload

value.definition: The explicit architectural-boundary test a Subordinate Payload must pass before becoming a top-level type, including class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record.

grounding.quote:
A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record
justifies its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as
payload detail (P3, P2; rc.2 #5b-promotion-test). A Subordinate Payload may
be promoted to a top-level type only when at least one of these is true:

value.label: Promotion Test

value.definition: Design debt in which subordinate payload detail becomes extra peer types without irreducible need: typing discomfort drives promotion, internal records become public without a new authoritative boundary, near-identical top-level types multiply where one family suffices, or one migration silently becomes parallel schema migrations.

grounding.quote:
Boundary Inflation exists when payload detail is promoted into peer types
because the code feels hard to type; internal records are turned into
public schema surface without a new authoritative boundary; many
near-identical top-level types appear for one boundary where one carrier
family would suffice; or one migration ticket silently becomes several
parallel schema migrations. Boundary Inflation is design debt, not
progress (P2).

value.label: Boundary Inflation

conditions: A realisation derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.
value.definition: An explicit derivation chain from constitutional WHAT through reference design, target Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping, target design mapping, target module boundary assets and implementation.

grounding.quote:
The required derivation
evidence is: (1) constitutional WHAT; (2) reference design; (3) target
Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping; (4) target design mapping; (5)
target module boundary assets; (6) implementation.

value.label: Reference-derived module design

value.definition: One complete design asset containing distinct domain, execution and lifecycle views, normally Mermaid classDiagram, sequenceDiagram and stateDiagram-v2. These fidelity-checked Ontology projections jointly form the sign-off surface for identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle and axiom conformance.
exceptions: A project may ratify another text-native format preserving the three distinct views and cross-view checks.

grounding.quote:
The views are not decorative and are not peer truth surfaces: they
are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology, and together
the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle
and axiom conformance (P1, P6).

value.label: Three-view design asset

value.definition: Durable design reasoning state that, together with the selected method basis, supports reconstruction of governing relations for a declared bounded action and its causally closed affected set. It is carried by existing Ontology evidence, matrices, frame declaration, views and module mapping rather than a separate documentation package.

grounding.quote:
The evidence above is not a documentation deliverable. It is the durable
reasoning state a bounded actor needs, because the actor selecting a local
action generally does not hold the reasoning that produced the governing
frames. Dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory and implementation
folklore are not that state

value.label: Invariant reconstruction sufficiency

value.definition: Source-defined action/relation decisions: preserves, changes, duplicates and violates. Their core values concern only the predicate that the action is admissible in the acting frame on the current governing basis.

grounding.quote:
The four decisions are a refinement of the core result algebra
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer what the
action does to one governing relation, and each maps to exactly one core
value for the predicate "the action is admissible in the acting frame on
the current governing basis"; the value travels with that predicate and
with the decision, whose meaning stays here

value.label: Action-to-relation decisions

value.definition: The structural domain projection of the Ontology, normally expressed as classDiagram.

grounding.quote:
The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology
(P1, P3; rc.2 #domain-model).

value.label: Domain model

value.definition: The behavioural projection of Ontology functions and authority, normally expressed as sequenceDiagram.

grounding.quote:
The `sequenceDiagram` is the behavioural projection of Ontology functions
and authority

value.label: Sequence model

value.definition: The lifecycle projection of Ontology entities, normally expressed as stateDiagram-v2.

grounding.quote:
The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities
(P3, P5; rc.2 #state-model).

value.label: State model

value.definition: Assessment of product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axioms across Ontology, authority, domain, sequence, state, native enforcement and admission/compiler evidence, with Verdict and Gap owner columns. Its source-defined verdicts are pass, fail and reasoned not_applicable; undecided evaluations can instead record direct core values.

grounding.quote: | Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |

value.label: Cross-view axiom evaluation

value.definition: Separate Ontology and design-pack acceptance decisions owned by the design authority. accepted denotes the accept disposition and maps to satisfied for the candidate's acceptance at its declared design-gate boundary; it is not an assessment result or an artifact-production result.

grounding.quote:
`accepted` is the disposition
`accept`, which maps to `satisfied` for "the candidate is accepted at its
declared boundary", the candidate being the Ontology or the design pack
and the boundary the design gate. A verdict that is not `accepted` is one
of the other three dispositions, mapped there, or no disposition yet,
which is no acceptance result.

value.label: Ontology and design acceptance

value.definition: A subordinate projection exposing abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings. It reveals repeated machinery that domain views can conceal, but cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority.

grounding.quote:
At a material semantic boundary, the design projects the
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings. The cross-view evaluation extends to prove that the domain views
and this projection describe one system

value.label: Computational realisation projection

value.definition: The explicit semantic and operational roles assigned by design authority to each material realisation component. Multiple roles are lawful; technological capability alone confers no authority.

grounding.quote:
A component's declared role set is design authority;
where a role carries authority, composition and use preserve the
applicable authority relation under IDENTITY §6, which is supporting law
here rather than the owner of the role model (P6). A component may
lawfully hold several roles.

value.label: Component role set

value.definition: An optional theoretical framing in which a Markov object is a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern with an effective blanket separating identity-bearing from context-bearing aspects. IACS, promotion, boundary inflation and strong boundary typing receive software-design analogies, not added prerequisites.

grounding.quote:
It treats a Markov object
as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose
effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is
load-bearing for context.

value.label: Markov-object theoretical framing

conditions: This profile governs the realisation boundary.
value.definition: Recommended role taxonomy: carrier modules define typed immutable contracts and values; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells perform external effects; projection modules derive views from source truth; binding/adapters translate boundaries without inventing law; constructor/materialisation modules produce artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Modules bound reasoning, expose ownership/consumption/emission/proof and make recurrence visible.
value.label: Module role taxonomy

value.definition: Typed values carrying source truth, preferably immutable, produced by constructors/parsers, transformed into new carriers or closed results and read by projections.
exceptions: Materially necessary mutation may be justified.

grounding.quote:
Source truth should be carried in typed immutable values unless mutation
is materially necessary (P3, P4b; rc.2 #7-immutable-carrier-rule). The
preferred shape: a constructor or parser produces a typed carrier;
transforms consume one carrier and return another carrier or a closed
result; projections read those carriers without mutating them.

value.label: Typed carrier

value.definition: Semantic-function outcomes are Product domain values, including unsupported or rejected outcomes; they are distinct from this method's core evaluation results. An evaluation consuming Product outcomes produces its own core value.

grounding.quote:
The outcome values a
semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

value.label: Product semantic-function outcome

value.definition: An explicit effect boundary, typically file writes, network calls, subprocess execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery or database mutation.

grounding.quote:
Typical effect edges include file writes, network calls, subprocess
execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and
database mutation.

value.label: Effect edge

value.definition: A hidden semantic centre is a controller, manager, service method, loop or wrapper whose implementation must be read to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth. Interface bleed is authority leaking between interface families through truth reconstruction, projection-as-closure, report/prompt-as-admission, wrapper decisions or meaning-inventing adapters.

grounding.quote:
A
module is acting as an unlawful semantic centre when reviewers have to
read it to discover what counts as closure, what identity means, what
failure means, what work is next, or what the current truth is. Those
meanings should already exist in carriers, contracts or explicit design
modules.

Interface bleed exists when one
interface reconstructs another interface's source truth; projection logic
becomes closure logic; report or prompt logic becomes admission logic;
public wrappers decide kernel semantics; or adapters invent meaning instead
of translating boundaries.

value.label: Hidden semantic centre and interface bleed

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
value.definition: Governance publishes state, structure, unmet pressure or unresolved identities, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and continuity. Strategy prescribes how another actor does work.
exceptions: Strategy ownership may be explicitly included in the boundary's ratified responsibility.

grounding.quote:
Lawful governance publication
includes current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure or unresolved
identities, route eligibility, the lawful edit or proof frontier, admitted
policy identity, and prior-turn or prior-run continuity.

value.label: Governance and strategy separation

conditions: The realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation.
value.definition: Improvement local to the active design/module boundary that preserves declared behaviour, ownership of truth, visibility and effects. It is subordinate to constitutional truth, declared module ownership and functional equivalence.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic
optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design
or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;
authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;
visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and
effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or
bootstrap doctrine.

value.label: Opportunistic optimisation

conditions: The same realisation pattern occurs across more than one processed boundary.
value.definition: A commonisation candidate rather than another purely local clean-up. Candidates are usually non-product truth, authority-neutral, repeated across at least two tickets/modules and usable through local adapters without changing ownership; examples include expectation derivation, nested contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect plans and non-semantic constructor helpers.

grounding.quote:
A recurrence candidate is usually not
product truth, authority-neutral, reused across two or more tickets or
module boundaries, and consumable through local adapters without changing
semantic ownership. Typical candidates include expectation derivation;
nested contract or policy carriers; proof-helper or fixture shaping;
effect-edge request or plan shaping; and constructor or materialisation
helpers that do not own semantic law.

value.label: Recurrence extraction and commonisation

conditions: A ticket applies this profile and claims its boundary has been processed.
value.definition: A bounded check against the accepted design and exact closure claim, reconstructing the complete selected function from requirements through Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, modules, implementation and module-owned proof. Its subject is the claim's causal closure, not the whole Product or construction history.

grounding.quote:
The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction.

value.label: Post-ticket bounded design review

value.definition: A new-looking interface forwarding to old authority, reconstructing missing truth from it, keeping it executable behind a new name or maintaining green proofs while old law still governs. Such substitution is bridge debt; intentionally retained compatibility is a separate bounded feature.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
proofs to stay green while the old law still governs. This is bridge debt,
not progress. If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof;

value.label: Proxy interface

value.definition: The subject's DESIGN_MODULE profile: a preferred realisation discipline for Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, authority/effect management and non-bleeding interfaces. Its engineering requirements are distinct from constitutional process, graph-native product law, release decisions and optional theoretical framing.

grounding.quote:
this profile what is
the preferred implementation design discipline when you want
Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, no interface bleed, and explicit
authority and effect management; and the UX profile the additional
discipline that applies when a module realises a UI surface.

value.label: DESIGN_MODULE profile

value.definition: The profile's review instruments: provenance-supported prompt clauses, 56 design review questions, a functional-realisation checklist and a compact hard gate. Questions and checks describe review obligations; they are not evidence that any implementation passed.

grounding.quote:
When reviewing code under this profile, ask (P6;
rc.2 #14-design-review-questions):

When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks (P6, P5;
rc.2 #14a-functional-realization-review-checklist):

value.label: Design review instruments

conditions: Consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution profile.
value.definition: Default identity generators, validators and normalisers for that realisation's own runtime surfaces and the default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers.

grounding.quote:
A consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution
profile may publish default identity generators, validators and

the exact predecessor immutable cut

value.definition: A realisation conforms to specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Semantic conformance uses the governing semantic basis as Σ.

conditions: A task builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor.
value.definition: A reconstruction return separates semantic conservation, demonstrated reduction and mere relocation. Relocation moves text between owners or carriers without changed meaning or a traced deciding-path change.

grounding.quote:

conditions: One specification may have several realisations.

exposure, the current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies,

the refinement that

predicate "a candidate is available". ACTIVATION §3 owns their grounds,

not new semantic dispositions, and none of them is an assessment or an
acceptance of the candidate (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).

The Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
the selected composition. The path is established early and widened in
bounded increments; where it already exists, the affected thread is extended
or revalidated. Increments are chosen for consequential uncertainty,
dependency and interface reach, and failure impact (P2; rc.2
#steel-thread-delivery; the generic sequencing heuristic is SPEC_METHOD §8).
