grounding.quote: The graph-native product and the project built with it are distinct.

value.label: Installed ODD builder

value.definition: Project built with the installed product, owning one stdo_<label>.json definition per distinct product WHAT; constitutional, local/collective reference-frame, realisation, work and composition locations; its constitutional surfaces; one or more realisation roots bound through how.build_tenants; and its own domain outputs/evidence. Software examples include design, code, tests, documents and proof. Clean installation is described as installing the builder, authoring target intent/definition/requirements/realisation root, then traversing the graph for domain outputs.

grounding.quote: - one `stdo_<label>.json` definition for each distinct product WHAT,

value.label: Target project

value.definition: Structural responsibility layer expressing a capability class, which the product binds to local domain semantics and GTL publishes as lawful transitions. Bootstrap/intake, design, implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and retrofit are example classes, not mandatory instance names.

grounding.quote:
A responsibility layer expresses one capability
class; the product binds that capability to its own local domain
semantics; the GTL carrier publishes the lawful transitions for that bound
capability (P1, P3).

value.label: Responsibility layer and local capability binding

value.definition: Audit of a move against current ODD profile law. For predicate 'the move complies with the current profile': compliant maps to satisfied because law is met; non-compliant maps to falsified through the violated law as counterexample; valid and worth incorporating maps to out_of_frame because required law is undeclared. Incorporation names the missing law, this profile as owner and required update, and is neither compliance nor failure.

grounding.quote: | valid and worth incorporating | out_of_frame | the current profile does not declare the law the move needs; the outcome names that law, this profile as its owner and the update it requires, which is the reconfiguration pressure of out_of_frame ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or indeterminate) |

value.label: ODD method audit and result mapping

value.definition: Product definition's what bindings locate authoritative WHAT: intent, product position, goals, requirements and scenarios. specification/ is the default software-development location.
value.label: Product specification WHAT

value.definition: Product definition's how bindings locate authoritative HOW, carrying design, GTL publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces. build_tenants/ is the default software-development location.
value.label: Product realisation HOW

value.definition: Runtime role owning traversal, dispatch, actor invocation, process supervision, graph-call realisation, runtime facts, runtime event emission and replay, frames, continuations, retry and correction control, closure folds over runtime truth, re-entry after publish boundaries, lineage and provenance.
value.label: ABG

value.definition: Domain product owning domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections, and domain closure and gap interpretation.

grounding.quote:
The ODD product owns domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the
published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections,
and closure and gap interpretation for its domain (P6, P1).

value.label: ODD product

value.definition: Service and query surfaces whose possible responsibilities are transport, sessions, routing, browser-safe projection and APIs; these responsibilities exclude runtime and continuation truth.

grounding.quote:
Service or query layers may own transport, sessions, routing,
browser-safe projection and API surfaces. They own neither runtime truth
nor continuation truth. The real constructive carrier is never hidden
behind the word service (P6).

value.label: Query and service layers

value.definition: Explicit typed domain assets or nodes, with concrete assets explicitly bound into typed domain boundaries and an asset_surface declaration at real produced or consumed boundaries.

grounding.quote:
Concrete assets must bind explicitly into
typed domain boundaries. Where an asset is a real produced or consumed boundary,
its `asset_surface` is declared (P3).

value.label: Typed assets and nodes

value.definition: Named GraphFunction or lawful graph-function composition carrying an operative constructive step; its public outer contract is distinguished from inner vectors and implementation.

grounding.quote:
Every operative constructive step is carried by one named `GraphFunction`
or one lawful graph-function composition.

value.label: Graph-function carrier

value.definition: Pre-implementation declaration of governed movement: source and target asset types, edge traversal or graph-function name, closure or evaluation obligation, lineage obligation, ambiguity or gap obligation, and allowed F_D, F_P and F_H bindings. Its declarative carrier comprises GTL graph functions, typed nodes, vectors, operator and evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy, projection and lineage-ledger declarations.

grounding.quote:
An outcome traversal declares the governed movement before
implementation: source asset type; target asset type; edge traversal or
graph-function name; closure or evaluation obligation; lineage obligation;
ambiguity or gap obligation; allowed `F_D`, `F_P` and `F_H` bindings. The
declarative carrier structure is GTL graph functions, typed nodes,
vectors, operator bindings, evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy
declarations, projection declarations and lineage ledger declarations
(P0, P3).

value.label: Outcome traversal and declarative carrier

value.definition: Machine-readable publication of retained functions, distinct from callable descriptions existing only in prose or prompt memory.

grounding.quote:
The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue. At
minimum each retained function should expose its name, inputs, outputs,
intent, and public or helper role. A callable surface that exists only in
prose or in prompt memory leaves the product under-built (P6, P3).

value.label: Function catalogue

value.definition: Operative publication surface for public graph-function carriers, their traversed graphs, typed node/vector surfaces, outer callable contracts and explicit refinement boundaries.

grounding.quote:
The product must publish the public graph-function carriers, the graph or
graphs those carriers traverse, typed node and vector surfaces, and the
semantic jobs or equivalent outer callable contracts bound to the public
carrier.

value.label: GTL module

value.definition: Visible current-state and query read models over admitted constructive history, carrier, runtime, event or source truth; their visibility is not replacement runtime authority.

grounding.quote:
Visible current state is a projection and does not replace runtime truth.
The ODD query lane may expose asset views, function catalogue views,
checkpoint overlays, provenance overlays and domain-specific
explainability overlays; it must not redefine ABG runtime facts (P3, P6).

value.label: Projection and query read model

conditions: An ODD product over GTL/ABG changes one of the listed execution-related surfaces.
value.definition: Pre-activation and pre-closure audit of execution ownership, including exactly-one-authority proof, a five-surface inventory and implementation-level evidence ruling out hidden execution authority.

grounding.quote:
An ODD product over GTL/ABG that changes runtime, `start` or `iterate`,
worker transport, actor invocation, process supervision, plugin dispatch,
event projection, closure, assurance, retry or continuation semantics
must include an execution-authority audit before activation and closure
(P6).

value.label: Execution-authority audit

conditions: ODD product over GTL/ABG.
value.definition: One framework-independent constructive homeostasis loop from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to lawful next action. It corrects toward required conditions as observations arrive, guarantees neither convergence nor adequacy of those conditions, and distinguishes the four externally defined diagnostic causes.

grounding.quote:
Every ODD product over GTL/ABG must preserve one constructive evaluation
loop running from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation
to the next lawful action. This is the profile's homeostasis loop, and
its constitutional surface names the operative functions directly:
`synthesize_model`, `eval_gap`, `evaluate_next` and `evaluate_action`
(P2, P5, P6). The loop is this profile's binding of
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation):
it corrects towards the required conditions as observations arrive,
guarantees neither convergence nor the adequacy of those conditions, and
its diagnoses distinguish the four causes named there (P2, P6).

value.label: Constructive evaluation and yield loop

value.definition: Loop input and observation domains: IntentLineage is admitted human, imported-source, prior-product, intent-engine or prior-construction-intent lineage backed by ABG event-log truth; ProductAssetModel is product-owned desired/known typed asset truth synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth, with admitted-event and product-projection publication refs; Worksite is workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and observed file/process substrate, not inherent authority; RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted ABG facts; RuntimeProjection is ABG replay-derived state over event log and execution basis; ObservationSnapshot is a read-only ABG evaluator view of runtime truth and relevant worksite facts with product domain rows; GapPressureRow gives product meaning to missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous assets/evidence over admitted observation.

grounding.quote:
| `ObservationSnapshot` | Read-only view of runtime truth plus worksite facts relevant to construction. | ABG evaluator carrier with product domain rows. |
| `GapPressureRow` | Typed pressure over missing, partial, blocked, waiting, or ambiguous assets and evidence. | Product domain meaning over admitted observation. |

value.label: Intent, model and observation carriers

value.definition: TargetObligationBinding binds gap pressure exactly to selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite/experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs and admissible graph outcomes; it is product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes for ABG consumption. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible product policy using the ABG evaluator kernel. ConstructionIntent is an admitted selection for one bounded graph invocation preserving outcome/bounded-basis refs, under ABG admission and traversal authority.

grounding.quote:
| `TargetObligationBinding` | Exact binding from gap pressure to the selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs, and admissible graph outcomes. | Product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. |
| `ActionCatalog` | Published lawful graph actions: graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs, and eligible outcomes. | GTL/product publication consumed by ABG. |

value.label: Binding, catalogue, priority and construction intent

value.definition: AdmittedEvidence comprises admitted worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence under ABG/product admission, never worker self-closure. EdgeFulfillmentLedger carries closure evidence and convergence for one edge attempt/version. EdgeClosureDecision is the closed sum close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice, block over that ledger. NextActionBasis distinguishes initial_selection, post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice and post_block; it is dispatch basis, not another controller, and post_reprice carries no action-selection authority. NextActionProjection is an ABG next-action read model over that basis and current truth with product policy, selecting only when lawful.

grounding.quote:
| `EdgeClosureDecision` | Sum type over the ledger: close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice, block. | Closure decision truth. |
| `NextActionProjection` | Read model that observes `NextActionBasis` plus current truth and selects a next graph action only when lawful. | ABG next-action evaluation projection with product policy. |

value.label: Evidence, ledger, closure and next-action carriers

value.definition: Four distinct authority functions: synthesize_model performs model synthesis; eval_gap discovers gaps read-only; evaluate_next selects next actions; evaluate_action evaluates the action just taken. Sharing implementation libraries does not merge their authority.

grounding.quote:
The loop has one model-synthesis function and three distinct evaluation
functions. They may share underlying libraries; they must not share
authority (P6):

value.label: Model synthesis and evaluation functions

value.definition: Subject-defined result distinctions: edge-obligation results from evaluate_action, action-selection no-action results from evaluate_next, candidate-availability step results, and candidate-acceptance dispositions answer different predicates. Closure decisions retain their domain vocabulary alongside exactly one cause-refined core value; they are not ACTIVATION dispositions accept, local_repair, re_enter or reject.

grounding.quote:
A closure decision is not a disposition and is never recorded
as one, and no disposition is a closure decision: `repair` is not
`local_repair`, and `re-enter` is not `re_enter`. Edge closure is
evidence toward acceptance and never acceptance itself

value.label: Closure, selection, availability and acceptance result domains

value.definition: Conforming agentic development combines an F_P walkthrough establishing that the constitutional process can be followed from minimal declared authority with an F_D artifact-admission gate establishing conformance of each produced act. The coder reasons, drafts and proposes; admission deterministically gates artifacts.

grounding.quote:
Conformance has two halves: an F_P proof that the process can be followed,
and an F_D gate that admits the produced artifacts (P6).

value.label: Agentic walkthrough and deterministic admission

value.definition: Graph-native proving surface for a feature/use-case boundary, pre-existing assets, traversed vectors, significant paths and closure evidence; declared scenarios and use cases are described as the best proving-path source because they pressure feature intent and design decisions.

grounding.quote:
Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces, not only test
documentation. A scenario bundle should make clear which feature or
use-case boundary is exercised; which assets are expected to exist before
the scenario starts; which vectors are expected to be traversed; which
significant paths are expected to be exercised; and what evidence closes
the scenario (P2, P6).

value.label: Scenario bundle

value.definition: ODD source-defined onboarding procedures: invocation sequence for building with ODD, cold-start reading order for concrete products, and ramp-up questions assessing whether the product is sufficiently ODD-shaped.

grounding.quote:
When an agent or designer is told `using ODD, build this product`, the
expected sequence is (P2, P0):

value.label: ODD invocation and onboarding

value.definition: Derived summary of the same-digest ODD member, sourced from §1, §2, §11.1–§11.5D, §11.7 and §11.7A. It summarizes graph-native authoring, outcome-first construction, ABG authority, evaluation, projection, manual explainability, yield and agentic admission; it owns no determination.

grounding.quote:
This section is a compression of this member, a derived surface in the
sense of [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition. Its sources are §1, §2, §11.1 to §11.5D, §11.7 and §11.7A of
this member at the same digest, and it owns no determination. Where it and
a source section differ, the source section decides

value.label: ODD canonical compression

value.definition: ODD's provenance account claims receipt and conservation of all 48 rc.2 ODD_METHOD rows under STDO-UP-015, with same modal force, exact formal blocks/tables and rewritten prose. It records successor member names, indicative-law/never restatements of imperatives, labelled rather than bold axiom titles, and British prose spelling with identifiers retained.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 ODD_METHOD.md received by this member, all 48 under
STDO-UP-015. Anchors are into rc.2 ODD_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of
this file. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own text at
the predecessor's modal force; a route is provenance only. Formal content
(code blocks and tables) is carried exactly and the prose around it is
rewritten.

value.label: ODD predecessor disposition account

value.definition: Guide owning the governed project's commentary layer: post purpose, authority boundary, location, identity, categories, structure, discussion state, posting rules and ratification. It consumes, without redefining, PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 comment binding, TICKETS §1 comments, SPEC_METHOD §2 authority surfaces and EVALUATION §1 claims/evidence. Shared-method adoption law belongs to SPEC_METHOD §6. Principle references P0–P6 and rc.2 routes are attribution/provenance, not dependence on that cut.

grounding.quote:
Guide. Owns the commentary layer of a governed project: what a post is
for, its boundary with authority, where posts live, their identity,
categories and structure, their discussion state, the posting rules and
ratification. Consumes
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)
(the `ticketing.comments` binding), [TICKETS §1](TICKETS.md#comments)
(comments among the work carriers), [SPEC_METHOD §2](SPEC_METHOD.md#2-the-chain)
(the surfaces that carry authority) and [EVALUATION §1](EVALUATION.md#1-claims)
(claims and evidence); defines none of them.

value.label: POSTING_GUIDE

value.definition: Working commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff or repricing confidence, potentially influencing later specification/design but not itself constitutional truth.

grounding.quote:
A post is not constitutional truth. It is working commentary, and it may
later influence specification or design (P6).

value.label: Post

value.definition: Closed category set: REVIEW critiques code/specification/design/posts; STRATEGY proposes technical or methodological direction; GAP identifies precise insufficiency/contradiction; SCHEMA describes data/event/interface/contract shape; HANDOFF transfers bounded context/task state; MATRIX compares decision options explicitly.
value.label: Post categories

value.definition: Discussion-state domain: Draft means the author is still shaping the post; Open means publication into active discussion; Closed means the discussion has concluded. Closed commentary is not ratification.
value.label: Post discussion state

value.definition: POSTING_GUIDE's predecessor account maps boundary→§2, location→§3, carrier identity→§4, categories→§5, structure→§6, discussion state/mutability→§7, posting rules→§8, ratification→§9, and shared-method adoption→SPEC_METHOD §6 with a local §10 pointer. It claims conservation of all listed content and modal distinctions, title prose restated in §1, imperative category/template headings restated with the same requirement, and Product authorization respelled authorisation.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 POSTING_GUIDE.md. Anchors are into rc.2 POSTING_GUIDE.md; a
locus is a section of this file unless another member is named. Every
conserved row is restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is
provenance only. Generalisations recorded here: imperative list headings
("Use these categories", "Use this base shape") are written as what a post
takes or uses, the same requirement; the predecessor's text under its
title, which no frontier row covers, is restated in §1; "Product
authorization" is written "Product authorisation" at SPEC_METHOD §6.

value.label: Posting-guide predecessor disposition account

value.definition: Tier-2 member owning project-to-method binding: overlay/layout independence, definition relations, constitutional sufficiency, installed basis/toolchain manager, semantic resolution, local binding, collective frames, WHAT/HOW/work carriers, recursive discovery/composition, conformance cases, STDO-SURFACE-001 and bootstrap. It adds no tier-1 definitions. Its owned contexts are product-definition-routing (§1–§4, §9, §12), semantic-resolution (§5, §6, §10) and build-tenancy (§8). Its schemas/templates/filenames/fields/commands are this Product's accepted interoperability realisations, not profile terms.

grounding.quote:
The schemas, templates, filenames, manifest
fields and commands named here are this Product's own realisation shapes,
accepted as interoperability boundaries under §11; they are not profile
terms. Three bounded contexts the predecessor placed in its SPEC_METHOD are
owned here: product-definition-routing (§1 to §4, §9, §12),
semantic-resolution (§5, §6, §10) and build-tenancy (§8).

value.label: PRODUCT_DEFINITION member

value.definition: JSON locator/relation overlay for one continuing current product WHAT in urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing under the selected complete STDO basis. The containing directory is the definition root. Relative URI references resolve against the definition file's retrieval URI; product.source_project separately identifies a source-project root.

grounding.quote:
This member owns the product-definition-routing bounded context,
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing`, under the selected
complete STDO basis, and defines that context's overlay, definition,
discovery, locator and composition concepts. The JSON schema named below
realises the accepted interoperability shape of the overlay and is not a
second semantic owner

value.label: Product-definition overlay

value.definition: Definition Label is the stable lowercase ASCII-letter/digit/hyphen/underscore filename suffix, unique only within a directory and not Product identity. Product-Definition Identity is product.definition_id, a URI identifying the mutable continuing WHAT-definition line, unique in the discovered workspace definition set, distinct from immutable Product and release identities.

grounding.quote:
The suffix `<label>` is the Definition Label: a stable lowercase local
discovery label of ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique
only among the definitions in the same directory. It is not Product
identity. The `product.definition_id` URI inside the definition is the
Product-Definition Identity: the stable identity of the mutable
product-definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition
set. It identifies one continuing WHAT definition, not one immutable
released Product (P3).

value.label: Definition Label and Product-Definition Identity

value.definition: F12 traces project-binding consequences to foundation commitments plus separately supplied instance premises: own authorities, chosen layout, shared workspace, recurring terms and released method. P0 is recovered; P1/P2/P3/P6 independent; P5 derives from P0/P6 with P0's open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with the non-reacquirability premise. Its ten rows distinguish consequences, owners of added domain/interoperability/policy choices, rule loci, pillars and consumers; it does not own the imported FOUNDATIONS rule.

grounding.quote:
The index also assigns to this family the rule of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members);
the table traces that rule in its sixth row, whose rule column names that
section, and owns none of it. Each commitment's standing is written as the
table of commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

value.label: F12 foundation-to-law family

value.definition: Complete selected governing-document set for a product, with no prescribed file count, collectively making recoverable axioms (starting truths, invariants, refusals), ontology (kinds, identities, relations, boundaries, lifecycle), epistemology (evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification, decision authority), taxonomy (classifications preventing category collapse) and semantics (terms, relations, states, operations, outcomes).

grounding.quote:
A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1; rc.2
#constitutional-set-sufficiency):

value.label: Constitutional Set

value.definition: Pair of immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI and installed-manifest SHA-256. The URI identifies an immutable annotated RC cut; the deterministic manifest binds tag object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. Its schema is schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json; it is transport/integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution.

grounding.quote:
The URI identifies one immutable annotated RC cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

value.label: Installed Release Basis

value.definition: Read-only deterministic acceptance object binding current Product Definition identity/bytes/current basis to a resolved immutable target cut, annotated tag object, commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is an operator-presentable acceptance token, not authority by possession. A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised fleet root and complete ordered per-definition plan-digest set.

grounding.quote:
An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

value.label: Adoption Plan and Fleet Adoption Plan

value.definition: Bounded executable realisation installing each immutable cut once in a shared versioned store, resolving logical release URIs to verified bytes, inventorying/verifying complete distributions, synchronising selected exact bases, producing digest-bound adoption plans and adopting only accepted plans, managing marker-bounded declared agent-file bootstrap, and applying these operations to explicitly discovered fleets.
value.label: STDO Toolchain Manager

value.definition: Operation evidence binding one explicitly selected Product Definition, the complete companion population of one exact upstream release-matched cohort, and owner-selected consumer bindings. The caller selects every native route and derived context in scope. Selection, plan and result are neither persistent dependency declarations nor registries nor locks; an empty derived-context population means the owner selected none.

grounding.quote:
A Complete Consumer Update Plan binds one explicitly selected Product
Definition and the complete companion population of one exact upstream
release-matched cohort to the consumer bindings selected by the
invocation's owner.

value.label: Complete Consumer Update Plan

value.definition: The selected Product Definition owns composition; the upstream cohort and each Product's release record own release and member identity.
value.label: Composition, release and member identity owners

value.definition: The separate cohort-update operation presents a whole plan without consumer effects, then may apply an explicitly accepted, re-derived plan. Its outcome predicates distinguish external effect, admission or construction availability, and conditions evaluated by commands with no intended external effect.

grounding.quote:
The separate `cohort-update` operation presents the whole plan without
consumer effects.

each
for its own predicate; the cause of an outcome selects its value, and the
mapping adds no core value

value.label: Complete update operation and outcome predicates

value.definition: For intended external effects, completed refines satisfied, not_effected refines falsified, and completion_unknown refines indeterminate. Whether the effect's end is established is a separate coordinate: a caught failure remains not_effected even when restoration is unverified. Unused staged immutable installs are recorded as the part that occurred.

grounding.quote:
Abrupt process or
  host loss, where no caught failure establishes that the update fell
  short, is `completion_unknown` (`indeterminate`), never `completed` or
  `not_effected`.

Whether its restored preimages are verified
  decides only whether the effect's end is established, never the value:

value.label: Manager effect result refinements

value.definition: A term is a lexical label in an occurrence, not a context-free concept identity. Every material occurrence has a semantic address: term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis and governed scope.

grounding.quote:
A term is a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept
identity.
(term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope)

value.label: Term occurrence and semantic address

value.definition: An explicitly identified semantic scope whose governed vocabulary, concepts and relations are jointly interpretable under named authority. PRODUCT_DEFINITION declares ownership of urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution under the selected complete STDO basis; glossary indexing does not participate in that declaration.

grounding.quote:
This member owns this law in the semantic-resolution bounded context,
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution`, under the selected complete
STDO basis.

A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope in
which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly
interpretable under named authority.

value.label: Bounded context

value.definition: An exact resolvable reference locating meaning owned by an authority under a selected basis; it creates neither meaning nor authority. GLOSSARY is a non-deciding locator index whose records point to exact clauses declaring contexts and owning concepts, without defining either or creating a shared default.

grounding.quote:
A concept reference is an exact,
resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected
basis; the reference locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor
its authority

The glossary defines neither and cannot
repair a missing declaration.

value.label: Concept reference and glossary locator

value.definition: Four explicit owner-authorised relation kinds: Semantic Import adopts unchanged meaning for a declared target scope; Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss, including specialisation; Semantic Equivalence requires governing authorities to establish equality while each concept retains its owner and context and neither adopts the other's meaning; Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating competitors. Translation, equivalence and disambiguation are not imports. A specialisation preserves declared source meaning while narrowing admissible instances or adding target-context constraints.

grounding.quote: | Semantic Disambiguation | not an import: it selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. Where the selected concept is owned in another bounded context, it enters that scope only by the import, translation or equivalence its carrier declares (§6) |

A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the
declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding
target-context constraints.

value.label: Cross-context semantic relation kinds

value.definition: A local axiom, override or disambiguation binds a source-owned decision through a URI, existing lawful authority, applicable overridden clause or resolved ambiguity, and exact scope. A local disambiguation additionally binds an exact lexical term, context, complete material candidate references, a selected member of those candidates, and every semantic basis required for the candidates and resolution. Overlay metadata locates the resolution and makes it checkable; the referenced URI owns it.
value.label: Local constitutional binding

value.definition: A Product-owned accepted declaration of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one governed Product scope or outcome. It binds exact reference-frame law and optional profile basis; admitting authorities and scopes; frames and evaluation inventory; actor-binding rules and capability envelopes; semantic, evaluation, operation and decision grants; result, conjunction, translation and coverage relations; lifecycle activation triggers and invalidation law. The non-empty reference_frame_bases set locates these declarations through URI, every admitting lawful authority and exact governed scope.

grounding.quote:
A Project Reference-Frame Basis is the Product-owned accepted declaration
of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one
governed Product scope or outcome

`reference_frame_bases` is the non-empty locator set for the accepted
frame bases through which finite actors collectively engage the governed
Product and its work.

value.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

value.definition: An execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable frame declaration or active configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope. The agent receives the REFERENCE_FRAME §11 activation packet and performs the ACTIVATION §1 step. An authorised ticket or work instruction carries the packet, while the Product Definition records the durable shared basis.

grounding.quote:
An Agent Frame
Activation is the execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable
frame declaration or active configuration, an exact evaluation, subject,
basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope;

value.definition: Work-carrier selection follows required lifetime: a durable ticket for identity across sessions, a sprint-local entry for traceability whose only value is inside the batch, or a run/return record for work confined to one activation. TICKETS owns the carrier model and smallest-lawful-carrier selection.

grounding.quote: The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime:

value.label: Lifetime-based carrier selection

value.definition: Four source-defined procedures cover substantive intake, feature introduction/change, project bootstrap or requirement-surface repricing, and gaps revealed by real use cases. Their ordering, conditional updates and design acceptance boundaries are represented as requirements rather than executed procedures.

grounding.quote:
only then treat the work as implementation, repricing or
release-bound change.

value.label: Change-management procedures

conditions: Under the selected complete basis.
value.definition: The substrate-neutral context urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance governs progressive disambiguation. Goals narrow priority and work-wave focus; intent direction and scope; product realisation shape and terms; requirements constitutional obligation; tenant/stack choice executable realisation class; design structural interpretation; implementation local detail. Major ambiguity materially affects architecture, stack, product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contract or downstream law; micro ambiguity is a local choice within an already-governed design boundary.

grounding.quote: `urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance`

value.label: Ambiguity governance

conditions: Declared policy permits bounded processing to carry or resolve declared ambiguity.
value.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing names bounded non-human processing permitted by policy. A person carrying or deciding ambiguity under policy without human-adjudication admission is governed by this processing's policy and recording requirements; performer identity does not determine operation kind.

grounding.quote:
is bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or
resolve declared ambiguity.

value.label: Lawful probabilistic processing

conditions: Authority admits explicit human judgment to resolve declared ambiguity where policy or risk appetite requires it.
value.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication names explicitly admitted human judgment. Admission makes the operation adjudication; merely relaying, recording or performing a step does not.

grounding.quote:
That admission makes an operation
human adjudication.

value.label: Human adjudication

value.definition: Recursive product lineage distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. The product definition is the source project's present-tense surface, distinct from the released artifact and active builder. Immutable v<version>-rc.<n> identifies an exact release cut; mutable v<version> discovers the highest-ordinal published cut. Calculus, subject interpretation and carrier encoding maintain independent content identities, judgments, supersession and proof obligations.

grounding.quote:
The only exact operative release identifier is the immutable release-cut
tag `v<version>-rc.<n>`

value.label: Product lineage and release identities

conditions: A reusable method change is proposed.
value.definition: Shared-method adoption expresses authority causality in this order: incident/review evidence, shared-method intake, one owning standard, consistency and independent review, human-authority acceptance, one complete released STDO version, explicit consumer selection, and consumer-owned realisation/evidence. It prescribes neither an intake workflow nor an artifact set.

grounding.quote:
The chain states authority causality. It prescribes no intake workflow and
no artifact set

value.label: Shared method adoption and propagation

conditions: A shared contract or carrier materially governs one or more listed truth-bearing functions.
value.definition: A core interface materially governs runtime closure, reporting/status truth, topology/frame progression, proof/qualification outcomes, event/projection semantics, identity/binding resolution, or provider/resolver behaviour. A change capable of altering how multiple surfaces determine present truth is a core-interface change.

grounding.quote:
If changing the
interface can alter how multiple surfaces decide what is true now, it is a
core interface change

value.label: Core interface

conditions: A change alters a load-bearing contract, carrier, resolver, provider, projection law, closure law or other interface shared by multiple surfaces.
value.definition: Core-interface migration is constitutional migration rather than an ordinary local patch. It replaces authoritative contract truth, migrates every impacted producer and consumer, and follows downstream effects until superseded closure law is gone.

grounding.quote:
the work is handled as a constitutional migration, not as incremental
patching

value.label: Constitutional core-interface migration

conditions: The project stays on the same implementation line and replaces authoritative source truth in place.
value.definition: Inside-out hard-break migration is one of two lawful constitutional strategies. It proceeds from the source carrier outward through deliberate breaks and repairs; bounded evolution is a rebuttable strategy-selection presumption, not a third strategy.
value.label: Inside-out hard-break strategy

conditions: A project intentionally abandons prior constitutional shape and re-derives on a new branch, version line or methodology basis.
value.definition: Fundamental migration is a constitutional reset. Fundamental re-adoption applies to a major rewrite on a materially different implementation basis, such as runtime, carrier, type system, substrate or realisation tree; prior implementation becomes reference material. Inherited constitutional material has adoption states adopted, superseded, deferred or orphaned. Inherited implementation is carry_across, materially unchanged and explicitly re-adopted; redundant, no longer needed; or rewrite, still needed but rebuilt under new requirements and design.

grounding.quote:
A fundamental migration is a constitutional reset, not an in-place
refactor.

the prior implementation is moved sideways
and treated as reference material, not live authority.

value.label: Fundamental migration and re-adoption

conditions: An affected product outcome is considered for promotion.
value.definition: The acceptance path is the outcome's full causal closure: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver, fallback, shared state surface, event, projection and proof surface capable of changing, interpreting or closing it. Singular authority concerns this entire closure, not one successful trace.

grounding.quote:
Singular authority means
one governing authority across that closure, not one selected successful
trace.

value.label: Outcome acceptance path

conditions: An intermediate product outcome is considered within an open migration.
value.definition: A product slice has identity and acceptance criteria derived from the product, every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained predecessor claim. Slice promotion is distinct from migration, qualification or release closure.
value.label: Intermediate product slice

value.definition: Projections, reports, status views and topology views reflect an authoritative carrier while remaining downstream of its truth and closure law.

grounding.quote:
Projections, reports, status views and topology views may reflect the
authoritative carrier; they do not become a second closure surface

value.label: Downstream projection

conditions: Refactor or migration affects mutable implementation surfaces.
value.definition: A transformation wave is the changing implementation across its declared affected scope. An inside-out migration wave is an ordered set of hard breaks over one interface family, not a mode permitting competing authority.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable
implementation surfaces
The migration wave is the ordered set of those breaks;

value.label: Transformation and migration wave

conditions: Construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker.
value.definition: Bounded execution applies ACTIVATION's step: accepted governing basis, bounded affected relations, selected computational relations, delegated execution and decision grants, construction/self-review, required independent live-surface assessment, owner disposition accept/local_repair/re_enter/reject, exact accepted checkpoint, and next already-authorised bounded action. Candidate availability, assessment results and owner disposition are separate results; preservation, progress and completion are distinct construction claims.

grounding.quote:
a candidate that is available or
assessed is not thereby accepted

value.label: Bounded construction step

conditions: A realisation claim requires closure evidence.
value.definition: Realisation evidence includes an authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible, and a present-tense statement of residual open pressure. This is an application of the TICKETS closure condition, not an additional closure condition.
value.label: Evidence for a realisation claim

value.definition: An ADR records a design decision boundary answering what design choice makes the acceptance criteria true. Each ADR file remains constitutional source; an optional registry is a read model. ADR history is append-only subject to explicit retirement.

grounding.quote: ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file;

value.label: Architecture decision record

conditions: Every product built with the described method.
value.definition: A build tenant is an independent project-owned HOW realisation of a product's WHAT. One WHAT has one or more independent tenants regardless of physical layout. A registry entry locates the tenant and is not its binding; tenant-local realisation remains derivative until governing truth is ratified in specification.

grounding.quote:
A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT.

value.label: Build tenant

value.definition: A product's requirements calculus comprises its WHAT obligations, permitted outcomes, and rules for refining and composing the work that realises it.

grounding.quote:
The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.

value.label: Requirements calculus

conditions: Operations, effects and resources are described insofar as material to obligations.
value.definition: A computational calculus declares executable operations, composition laws, permitted transformations, effects and resource behaviour.

grounding.quote: A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,

value.label: Computational calculus

value.definition: An execution environment concretely performs operations through a technology stack, a human process of people, roles, documents, communication channels and decision procedures, or both. Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess, relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority it requires.

grounding.quote:
An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations:

value.label: Execution environment and operation kinds

value.definition: A tenant binding consists of a calculus binding from requirements calculus to computational calculus and an execution binding from computational calculus to execution environment. Both are tenant-owned design and realisation, declared in existing design/realisation surfaces and recorded as design decisions without a further mandatory carrier. Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts remain distinct across the binding.

grounding.quote: A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts:

value.label: Build-tenant binding

value.definition: The source-disposition register records claimed conservation, generalisation, relocation, new law and proposed supersession of predecessor rows. Anchors point to predecessor material and loci to receiving sections; routes are provenance, not imported authority. Conserved rows are stated to be restated by their receiving members.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is
restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance only.

value.label: Predecessor source-disposition register

value.definition: TICKETS is a tier-2 member owning goals, tickets, sprints, comments and execution contracts as one carrier model; layout/bindings; sprint and ticket mechanics; triage/class recording/upward propagation; carrier selection and carrier-side contract admission; execution/verification separation; J/O continuity; closure/reuse; test-case authority; migration ticket declaration/checklist/review; one-truth projections; recommended shapes and operating mode. It is the T area and realises FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION, without redefining their law.

grounding.quote:
Tier 2. Owns the work carriers of the method: goals, tickets, sprints,
comments and execution contracts as one model;

value.label: TICKETS member

value.definition: The goals carrier is the current epic layer located by ticketing.goals, default GOALS.md. It states the active work wave and present priorities, broader than a ticket and narrower and more current than intent; it is not durable execution tracking.

grounding.quote:
Goals are
not the durable unit of execution tracking

value.label: Goals carrier

conditions: Work needs independent durable identity, including features, bugs, spikes and chores.
value.definition: A ticket is one enduring, typed work record and the source of truth for its work unit, durable across sessions. One Markdown file is the default carrier; bugs and features share this system.

grounding.quote: Tickets are the enduring work records. Each ticket is one durable record,

value.label: Durable ticket

value.definition: A TICKETS sprint is one manifest for a bounded execution batch and its explicit close review, located by optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/. It batches authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and local compliance debt. It can contain durable tickets, manifest-local iterations, or both; its batch authority is not constitutional authority.

grounding.quote: Sprints are not constitutional authority:

value.label: Sprint work carrier

value.definition: Comments are POSTING_GUIDE posts for ideas, strategy, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries and reasoned decisions. ticketing.comments.root locates the message board, default .ai-workspace/comments/. Comments have no task-status authority or decision authority of their own.

grounding.quote:
A decision recorded in a
comment takes its authority from the surface that owns the decision, once
it is adopted there

value.label: Comment carrier

value.definition: An execution contract is the admitted run-scoped execution function derived from a ticket, a sprint manifest plus included ticket/iteration, or intake when no durable or sprint-local identity is needed. It lives for one run, unlike a ticket across sessions/work waves or a sprint through its batch and close review; it is neither a rival backlog nor a second planning surface.

grounding.quote:
Execution contracts are not a
rival backlog or a second planning surface

value.label: Run-scoped execution contract

conditions: A ticket uses closure-bearing milestones.
value.definition: A milestone is a bounded work claim with stable identity, dependencies, current state, required evidence and explicit relation to ticket closure. Several milestones may belong to one ticket without creating several tickets.

grounding.quote:
Each milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim,
relevant dependencies, current state, required evidence, and an explicit
relation to ticket closure

value.label: Closure-bearing milestone

value.definition: Product-definition bindings locate carrier authority: ticketing.goals for epics; optional ticketing.sprints.root for batches/close review; ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed for ticket authority; ticketing.comments.root for publication/discussion. stdo_default.json supplies the starter layout with specification/GOALS.md and .ai-workspace/{sprints,tickets/{backlog,active,completed},comments/<agent-id>}. The definition locates carriers without owning their ticket/comment content.

grounding.quote:
The definition locates these carriers and
does not own their ticket or comment content.
The starter file layout (P2, P3; rc.2 #default-layout):

value.label: Carrier bindings and default layout

value.definition: Each sprint has one durable manifest record. A Markdown file is default; other bound carriers preserve identity, required fields, history, closure law and one-truth relation. A local filename should have a stable ID and short slug; the dated SPRINT examples are recommendations.

grounding.quote: Each sprint has one durable manifest record;

value.label: Durable sprint manifest

value.definition: Minimum sprint statuses are active, admitting iteration within the boundary; closing, freezing new iteration while close review/paydown classification run; closed, review finished and remaining debt accepted, ticketed, repriced or removed; and superseded, an incorrect boundary replaced by a new authority surface, sprint or ticket set. Optional planned/cancelled states do not replace close review.

grounding.quote:
A project may add `planned` or
`cancelled`; those states do not replace close review.

value.label: Sprint status domain

conditions: The governing method allows local proof deferral and all escrow conditions hold.
value.definition: Compliance escrow is visible local compliance debt held by a sprint rather than acceptance. It does not satisfy method, release or product closure until paid down, accepted under governing method, or repriced.

grounding.quote:
Deferred compliance is not
silent debt: it is escrow held by the sprint,

value.label: Sprint compliance escrow

value.definition: Review at the sprint close boundary under the authority cited by its manifest. Its item classifications and debt outcomes are results; completing this review does not require every outcome to be satisfied.

grounding.quote:
Each classification
takes exactly one core value, for the predicate "the reviewed item is
accepted as compliant under the sprint authority"

value.label: Sprint close review

value.definition: The six item outcomes are accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice and remove. Debt-entry outcomes are accepted, ticketed, repriced and removed. Each maps to one core value at its close boundary; the repricing layer is a declared change-class fact accompanying the value as domain outcome.

grounding.quote:
Each reviewed item is classified as one of `accepted` (compliant under the
sprint authority), `local_paydown` (local debt remains and is captured by a
paydown ticket), `design_reframe` (the work needs design repricing),
`requirement_reprice` (the work needs requirement repricing),
`product_reprice` (the work changes product definition) or `remove`

value.label: Close classifications and debt outcomes

value.definition: A durable unit of work with one authoritative record, stable identity and lifecycle. Its default carrier is one markdown file.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is
one markdown file. A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only
when it preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition,
stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal
local copy

value.label: Ticket

value.definition: One admitted upstream work item with more than one build-tenant execution line, within urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy. The member owns its work-item/ticket-lifecycle relation, while PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 supplies the context and tenant identities; build-tenant identity and realisation meaning are not redefined here.

grounding.quote:
A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more
than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.

value.label: Multi-build-tenant work item

value.definition: A ticket carrying one tenant-local execution lifecycle, distinct from upstream authority and sibling tenant tickets. Its build_tenant identifies the applicable product how.build_tenants entry.

grounding.quote:
The
`build_tenant` value identifies the
applicable entry in the product's `how.build_tenants` definition; a path
name, display alias or tracker label does not replace that identity unless
the product definition binds it as the identity.

value.label: Tenant-local ticket

value.definition: The kind of work record. The minimum common type set is feature, bug, spike and chore, expected to suffice for most cases but extensible by a project.

grounding.quote:
The minimum common set of ticket types is `feature`, `bug`, `spike` and
`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for
most cases

value.label: Ticket type

value.definition: The execution or migration discipline governing a ticket. Its minimum common set is ordinary and implementation_migration, either available to feature, bug, spike or chore.

grounding.quote:
Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type: type answers what kind of
work record this is; category answers what execution or migration
discipline governs the ticket (P3, P1; rc.2 #ticket-category). The minimum
common set is `ordinary` and `implementation_migration`, so a `feature`,
`bug`, `spike` or `chore` may carry either.

value.label: Ticket category

value.definition: A ticket category for governed replacement of one implementation truth path by another across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces. Examples include replacing tracker/read-model authority, migrating every producer and consumer to a new public interface before closure, and removing a bridge or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

grounding.quote:
`implementation_migration` is
used when the ticket is not "change code until tests pass" but a governed
replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,
consumers, projections and proof surfaces

value.label: Implementation migration ticket

value.definition: The intake-declared lawful constitutional re-entry class, using SPEC_METHOD §4. Common, non-exhaustive pairings are feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor. A spike remains exploratory but carries its current triage class.

grounding.quote:
Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of
work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully
re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`
declared by intake triage, using the classes of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes)

value.label: Change class

value.definition: Declared carrier states include ticket statuses, local added states, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and change_class. Minimum ticket statuses are backlog, active and completed. They are not evaluation results and map to no core value.

grounding.quote:
The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes).

value.label: Declared carrier state

value.definition: Backlog is accepted durable work outside current execution focus that should remain visible; active is the current bounded execution set; completed is closed work retained as history. Product bindings ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed locate these lanes, defaulting respectively to .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/, active/ and completed/. The separation keeps live search small and readable without relocating deferred work into goals or comments.

grounding.quote:
`backlog`
is accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part of the
current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

value.label: Ticket lanes

value.definition: Family F13 concerns which carrier holds work, what it may claim and when it closes. Instance premises are differing lifetimes, multiple apparent state surfaces, multiple build tenants, migrations between authoritative truth paths and variable carrier technologies. The table presents attributed consequences and separately owned policy choices; it does not decide beyond cited rules.

grounding.quote:
This family (F13 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides which record carries a piece of work, what that record may claim
and when the work closes.

value.label: F13 work-carrier family

value.definition: One run-scoped contract for each execution governed by the represented method, derived from the smallest lawful carrier selected by work/obligation lifetime after establishing upstream authority. Ticket-shaped means execution-contract fields, not a durable ticket identity or lane state. Contract states include drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded.

grounding.quote:
Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below.

the contract carries at minimum the states named in ACTIVATION §1
(drafted, admitted, rejected, superseded).

value.label: Execution contract

value.definition: The local gain function of the work: evaluation_criteria express progress/completion and non_closure_conditions express failures that remain despite locally green proof.

grounding.quote:
An execution contract should expose both what counts as progress or
completion and what still counts as failure even when some local proof is
green. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and
`non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for
the work

value.label: Evaluation criteria and non-closure conditions

value.definition: Ticket and work-instruction terms resolved under PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. Their relevant bounded-context meaning depends on the cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis and affected scope.

grounding.quote:
Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning

value.label: Bounded-context work-term binding

value.definition: The explicit declaration and live markdown checklist constituting ticket-local authority for implementation migration. Strategy values are inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption; library_usage values are none, consume and extend.

grounding.quote:
A ticket with `ticket_category: implementation_migration` carries both an
explicit migration declaration block and a hard migration checklist. Both
are part of the ticket authority, not optional commentary.

value.label: Migration declaration and checklist

value.definition: The review of repeated realisation patterns and the declaration of boundary-local rebuilding, consumption of an existing reusable library/commonisation surface, or extension of that surface before local implementation lands.

grounding.quote:
An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local
implementation lands; `library_usage` records which

value.label: Recurrence and library review

value.definition: A named walk of every live interface able to bypass, reinterpret, replay or project migrating truth, with an interface-specific closure condition for every item.

grounding.quote:
For a core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration, the
ticket includes an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be
used as closure evidence. The checklist is a named walk of every live
interface that can still bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the
migrating truth path

value.label: Impacted Interface Review Checklist

value.definition: An assessment distinct from construction and owner acceptance. The reviewer is not the reviewed subject's author; a constructor's self-review remains construction evidence. Generic assessment, acceptance and closed-result reuse are attributed respectively to EVALUATION §3, EVALUATION §5 and ACTIVATION §7.

grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).

value.label: Independent assessment

value.definition: A residual judgment needed by another activation, recorded once with its owning work and distinguished from a direct or lawfully proxied owner ruling. C, J and O are referenced SPEC_METHOD annotations; J is not O.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5.

value.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

value.definition: An obligation's owner-set post-repricing standing: retained, superseded, deferred or withdrawn. These are recorded states, not assessed-candidate acceptance results or qualified predecessor-claim dispositions, and map to no core value.

grounding.quote:
The four repricing dispositions are recorded states of the obligation,
set by its owning authority; they are not results and map to no core
value.

value.label: Obligation repricing disposition

value.definition: A bounded claim whose completion is governed by evidence for every applicable obligation, applicable required judgments and owner rulings, absence of active non-closure conditions and any reserved owner acceptance. This member owns the work-claim closure condition; SPEC_METHOD §4 applies it to a change span.

grounding.quote:
A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains.

value.label: Work claim

value.definition: A proof projection from admitted work authority. A substantive test should derive through ticket, intake triage, lawful re-entry, governing requirement/design/module/published function/carrier/closure surface and then expectation. Implementation behaviour is evidence, not the authority for expected results.

grounding.quote:
ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation

value.label: Test case

value.definition: One work-state authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, tickets their state, milestone authority subordinate milestones and accepted design realisation decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections.

grounding.quote:
Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections

value.label: Work authority chain and projections

value.definition: Three recommended document shapes: sprint manifest, ordinary ticket and migration ticket. They illustrate required fields and sections without instantiating the illustrated work. The sprint example carries id/status/goal/timestamps, Authority, Scope, Excluded Boundaries, Expected Change Classes, Iterations and Closure. The ordinary example carries ticket fields, Context, Acceptance and Links. The migration example carries ticket/migration fields, Migration Declaration and the live Migration Checklist.

grounding.quote:
These shapes are the recommended carriers of the fields and sections the
rules above require; a project may bind another shape that carries the
same fields

value.label: Recommended carrier templates

conditions: The default local-file carrier is used.
value.definition: Humans and agents can read the active folder directly; backlog remains searchable durable work outside immediate focus; rg suffices for locating active work, without a required database or board. Illustrative commands search headings/status/type/goal in active and backlog folders, and T-001/B-002 identities across tickets.

grounding.quote:
The default local-file carrier assumes that humans and agents can read the
active ticket folder directly; that backlog remains searchable durable work
without competing with the active lane for immediate attention; that `rg`
is sufficient for finding active work; and that no database or board is
required

value.label: Local-file operating mode

value.definition: An attributed provenance ledger routing received rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md anchors to this member or named other members. It claims conserved rows are restated locally and labels heading-only predecessor rows inapplicable. It records new close-result mappings, declared-state distinctions and a foundation table; routes are provenance only, not independent decisions or evidence that conservation was verified.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md received by this member. Anchors are into
rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless another
member is named. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

value.label: Ticket source-disposition ledger

conditions: Its instance rules apply where a Product adopts this optional profile.
value.definition: Tier-3, application-neutral model-family signature for immutable application histories over an externally changing subject. Stable identity urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile, owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:traversal-occurrence-profile. It imports one exact a_c basis and its laws without amending the calculus, becoming universal to its models or defining a universal execution theory.

grounding.quote:
Tier 3. The `a_c` traversal occurrence profile over mutable subjects: an
optional model-family signature for immutable application histories. It
imports [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md) by reference under
[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of it

Adoption is optional. The profile imports one exact `a_c` basis and
instantiates one closed model-family signature under that basis's record
and model laws. It does not amend `a_c`, does not become part of every
